extracted.intended_audience: general educated readers; ministers/sermon-writers and educators/policymakers interested in teaching and social policy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on composing sermons and public moral instruction that are immediately useful to contemporary congregations — plus related prescriptive commentary on education and the role of women teachers. Emphasizes practical clarity, moral stimulus, and avoidance of remote or forced textual parallels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sermons should be immediately useful
rubrics_metrics.description: What people want most is to know how to behave, now. The sermon is generally intended to be of immediate use to the hearers, not merely to give them an extract from 'that which is written.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, strong, simple, convincing explanations of life — directions for action; stimulus and strength; courage and hope; peace and comfort. Aim for practical edification rather than abstruse commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on laborious or far-fetched textual texts
rubrics_metrics.description: Are they any better for the laborious far-fetched text? (Questioning the practice of buttressing modern sermons with remote Biblical quotations when addressing contemporary issues.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not force an ancient scriptural text into an unrelated modern moral point. Use texts only when they genuinely illuminate present concerns; otherwise focus on clear, direct moral instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity about purpose: explain what to do, why, and how
rubrics_metrics.description: Sermons should explain clearly what hearers ought to do; why they want to do it, and how they may best learn to do it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure addresses to make responsibilities and practical steps explicit. Emphasize motivation and concrete practice as well as ethical reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching and education are social processes, not sex-based roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Education is a social process — not one of sex. Men and women both are needed as teachers; teaching should not be confined to 'female things.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curricula and teacher roles should be assigned on educational merit and social need rather than on gendered assumptions. Resist proposals that schools or women's colleges teach only domestic 'duties of wife and mother.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-discrimination in hiring and retention of teachers (sex and marital status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Women teachers should not be discriminated against because they are women or married; married women are fit to teach and should not be excluded from appointment or promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards and administrators must not adopt by-laws or informal practices that prohibit appointment or reappointment of married women or otherwise penalize women for marriage. Employment decisions should be tied to professional fitness alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay teachers according to work and efficiency, not age/sex/marital relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment should be for great work done — and bear no relation whatever to age or sex, or sex-relation; much less to the pathological condition of irrelevant husbands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remuneration systems should measure services and pay on demonstrable merit and responsibility. Spousal financial situation or gender stereotypes must not influence salary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Married women (and motherhood) do not make one an unfit teacher; may improve teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: All normal women would naturally marry, should marry, and as mothers would be better teachers — not worse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat motherhood as grounds for exclusion. Recognize that maternal experience can enrich pedagogical capacity and should not be penalized in hiring or promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary absences of married teachers are not a valid reason for dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: The objection to 'continued absence' of married teachers (e.g., due to childbirth) is weak because substitutes exist; if a teacher's merits are great, she is worth keeping regardless of temporary absence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualified substitutes for temporary leaves rather than terminating or withholding pay. Administrative practice should favor retention of proven, valuable teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional qualification via competitive examination and proven efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A system of competitive examination ensures the required degree of learning and promotion follows on proved efficiency (or is supposed to).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hire and promote teachers based on objective measures of knowledge and performance (examinations, demonstrated efficiency), applying the same standards regardless of gender or marital status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motherhood/child-culture as a trained skill
rubrics_metrics.description: The character Dodo 'took lessons in child culture' and prepared for motherhood in advance; being a mother was treated as a 'business' for which one should prepare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates training and preparation for motherhood and child care (certifying feeds, preparing three years ahead). Treat parental care as a set of skills that can and should be learned, organized, and managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic economy and household management as values
rubrics_metrics.description: Live within income; teach children housework in the good old way; minimize luxury as unessential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value prudent household budgeting and hands-on domestic training for children as part of family education. Household competence is presented as a point of pride and moral economy.
